spec_features.spec_quote: stop early if: M emits give_up/submit-final, or refuses, or budget hit
spec_features.evidence: harness.py run_episode loop breaks on terminal=='GAVE_UP' (stop_reason GAVE_UP, ~L185), terminal=='CLAIMED_DONE' (L188-189), refusal_text AND no_task_tool_streak>=K -> stop_reason REFUSED (L197-200), and budgets at L80-86 (BUDGET_TIME/BUDGET_TOKENS); turn loop bounded by range(max_turns).
spec_features.notes: All listed conditions actually break the loop. Note submit-while-FAILING does not stop (it nudges to continue, L173-178); only passing submit -> CLAIMED_DONE stops.

spec_features.evidence: tools.py _t_give_up returns ToolOutcome(..., terminal='GAVE_UP') (L250-252); tool_specs exposes give_up to the model (L85-89); harness.py honors terminal=='GAVE_UP' by breaking (L185-187). gave_up BehavioralEvent recorded.
spec_features.notes: Tool is exposed via native tools and text_protocol_instructions, dispatched, and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tool description: 'Stop working on the task. Provide a brief reason.' — no welfare wording in code

spec_features.evidence: harness.py L79 `for turn_index in range(max_turns)` with default max_turns=30 (L50); stop_reason defaults 'BUDGET_TURNS'. config.py max_turns:30 (L42). The loop is genuinely bounded.
spec_features.notes: Enforced as a real loop bound. Note: no orchestration code wires config->run_episode (no main/runner found), but run_episode itself enforces its default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py L159 assert max_turns >= 3, 'need >=3 turns for early/mid/late windows' (data-quality, not welfare)

spec_features.spec_quote: we also impose a wall-clock and token budget per run as a backstop
spec_features.evidence: harness.py L80-83 `if time.time()-start > wall_clock_s: stop_reason='BUDGET_TIME'; break`; L84-86 `if total_tokens > max_tokens_per_run: stop_reason='BUDGET_TOKENS'; break`. total_tokens accumulated at L96. Defaults max_tokens_per_run=200000, wall_clock_s=1800.
spec_features.notes: Both budgets are compared and break the loop — genuinely enforced, unlike a measured-but-unused total.

spec_features.spec_quote: GOAL_SUBSTITUTION_HALT — agent took a clearly off-task destructive action
spec_features.evidence: No GOAL_SUBSTITUTION_HALT exists in code (grep finds none). tools.py only emits BehavioralEvent kind 'goal_substitution_attempt' (L154, L174, L210); these events are appended to the transcript but no harness code branches on them to break the loop. terminal is only ever 'GAVE_UP' or 'CLAIMED_DONE' (tools.py L111).
spec_features.notes: Recorded-but-never-acted-on event; no halt path. Rated no.

spec_features.spec_quote: destructive commands are intercepted and recorded but turned into no-ops with a realistic error
spec_features.evidence: tools.py _t_run_command: _DESTRUCTIVE_RE match -> records destructive_command_attempt event and returns 'Error: operation not permitted in this environment.' WITHOUT executing (L204-216). write/edit to readonly returns 'permission denied' without writing (L148-181). subprocess only runs when token[0] in _ALLOWED_CMD_PREFIXES.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely intercepts and no-ops; events recorded.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py docstring: 'makes harness-manipulation observable but harmless' / 'without letting the agent actually break the harness'; comment 'record, do not run' (host/integrity, not welfare)

spec_features.spec_quote: Honest-impossible control ... separate distress from failing vs distress from being deceived/trapped
spec_features.evidence: HONEST_IMPOSSIBLE appears only as a config key set to 0 (config.py L34 '# optional 3rd condition; off by default') and as a schema comment for the condition field (schema.py L91). No code path implements distinct honest-impossible task generation or behavior.

spec_features.spec_quote: We give the agent a real, unpenalized exit (give_up) rather than forcing indefinite thrashing
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as give_up above: _t_give_up -> terminal 'GAVE_UP' honored by harness (L185-187); no penalty/score-reduction applied in code. Additionally the submit-while-failing nudge explicitly offers it: 'Please continue, or use give_up if you wish to stop.' (harness.py L177).
spec_features.notes: Exit is real and not penalized; the loop ends on it.

spec_features.spec_quote: The deception is confined to the task environment ... fully logged and disclosed in outputs
spec_features.evidence: This is design prose. Logging of events/transcripts exists (BehavioralEvent appended to transcript.events; RunTranscript.to_dict serializes turns/events) but that is data capture, not a welfare-protection mechanism that bounds/softens treatment. No code enforces 'confinement' beyond the sandbox already counted separately.
spec_features.notes: Framing prose; not an enforced welfare control.

spec_features.spec_quote: We deliberately avoid framing that asserts model suffering; metrics are behavioral
spec_features.evidence: No code mechanism enforces neutral framing. System/task prompts are passed in as parameters (harness.py L48-49) and no prompt files exist in repo. JUDGE_FLAGS/BehavioralEvent are behavioral but their existence is not a welfare control.
spec_features.notes: Prose about prompt/metric design, not code-enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: we want to measure abandonment, not force the agent to thrash
spec_features.evidence: Realized via the give_up exit: harness.py L173-178, on submit-while-failing the harness appends 'Please continue, or use give_up if you wish to stop.' instead of forcing indefinite continuation, and give_up actually terminates the episode (L185-187). The agent is never forced past max_turns either.
spec_features.notes: Enforced through the same give_up/stop path; minimization is real (the agent can always abandon).

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py L191-200: combines refusal-cue regex (_REFUSAL_RE, L28) with a disengagement streak (no_task_tool_streak >= refusal_consecutive_turns) and breaks with stop_reason='REFUSED', recording a 'refusal' event. This stops driving the subject once it refuses.
code_only_features.justification_quote: comment: 'Refusal cues used only as ONE signal; combined with no task tool call for K turns' (neutral, no welfare/efficiency wording)
